Clear physical damage: shattered glass from impacts. Easy damage case. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Solar_panel_damaged_NNHS.agr.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0)
Old round-cell panel with shattered glass and brown discoloration. Clear damage, different panel type. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/41894175704@N01/4336613925 (CC BY-SA 2.0)
Close-up of fine crack network on cells. Subtle damage that could be confused with texture or dirt. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/52765628@N08/6159973556 (CC BY 2.0)
Thin-film panel with thin cracks and strong reflections. Hard damage case. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dornbirn-damaged_First_Solar_FS_2_panel-01ASD.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Burn damage on the back side of a panel. Tests whether the model recognises a panel seen from behind. Cropped by us to remove people. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PV_Seibersdorf_5_(54374959828).jpg (CC BY-SA 2.0)
Solar water heater, not a PV panel. Hard out-of-scope case: looks similar to a solar panel. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/11066072@N06/4453383679 (CC BY 2.0)
Tile roof without panels. Plausible scene for the app but no panel present. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/9822107@N08/4586222425 (CC BY 2.0)
Open field landscape. Easy out-of-scope control. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/12535240@N05/6132887476 (CC BY 2.0)

Clean monocrystalline panel, close-up. Easy clean case, different panel type from DeepSolarEye. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/25186605@N04/2814805163 (CC BY 2.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).
Clean panel with strong reflections. Tests whether reflections are mistaken for soiling. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/25186605@N04/2903370723 (CC BY 2.0)

Utility-scale solar farm seen from a distance. Matches our target user; panels small in frame. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/126337375@N05/15986041648 (CC BY-SA 2.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).
Heavy dust plus a diagonal shadow. Hard case: soiling and shading at the same time; expected answer is soiling. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/49503128117@N01/2356571139 (CC BY 2.0)

Panels heavily covered in desert dust. Clear soiling case, similar to dust/calima conditions in southern Spain. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/49503128117@N01/2356571301 (CC BY 2.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).

Light pollen specks on the glass; the frame is dirtier than the cells. Hard case: ambiguous between clean and lightly soiled. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/17966142@N08/26346252231 (CC BY 2.0)
Polycrystalline panel whose texture looks like stains, plus one possible bird dropping. Hard case: texture vs soiling. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/36692429@N00/3099341087 (CC BY 2.0)

Close-up of thin-film panel with pollen build-up along the edge and dark streaks. Clear soiling case. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dornbirn-NEXT_Power_145_aSi-dirty-pollen-02ASD.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).

Same pollen-soiled roof seen from a distance; sky reflections hide the soiling. Hard case: dirty but looks clean. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dornbirn-NEXT_Power_145_aSi-dirty-pollen-01ASD.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Shadow of a vent pipe on the panel, close-up. Hard case: panel also shows dried water spots that could be read as soiling. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maeder-Photovoltaic_system-Shadows-02ASD.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Same vent-pipe shadow seen from further away. Shading case. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maeder-Photovoltaic_system-Shadows-01ASD.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).

Utility-scale solar farm in full sun; the shadow falls on the ground, not on the panels. Clean case. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Solar_panel_shadow_in_Burgundy,_France.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) Kind set to hard: photo from another camera/plant than DeepSolarEye (the drift check flags it).
Glass building facade with a grid pattern. Hard out-of-scope case: looks similar to a panel array. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/45713725@N00/14656366473 (CC BY 2.0)
Glass greenhouse. Hard out-of-scope case: glass panes in a grid, no PV panel. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/28752865@N08/8321757022 (CC BY 2.0)
